question: What are the top 3 best-selling product variants by completed order revenue within each top-level category?
sql:
WITH category_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        COALESCE(pcat.name, cat.name) AS parent_category,
        cat.name AS subcategory_name,
        p.name AS product_name,
        pv.sku_variant,
        SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold,
        SUM(oi.line_total) AS total_revenue,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY COALESCE(pcat.name, cat.name) 
            ORDER BY SUM(oi.line_total) DESC
        ) AS sales_rank
    FROM public.order_items oi
    JOIN public.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN public.product_variants pv ON pv.variant_id = oi.variant_id
    JOIN public.products p ON p.product_id = pv.product_id
    JOIN public.categories cat ON cat.category_id = p.category_id
    LEFT JOIN public.categories pcat ON pcat.category_id = cat.parent_category_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'completed'
    GROUP BY pcat.name, cat.name, p.name, pv.sku_variant
)
SELECT parent_category, subcategory_name, product_name, sku_variant, total_units_sold, total_revenue, sales_rank
FROM category_sales
WHERE sales_rank <= 3
ORDER BY parent_category, sales_rank
notes: Tests multi-hop join (5 tables), category self-join for top-level resolution, and DENSE_RANK() window function partitioned by parent category.

question: Which top 10 repeat customers with at least 3 completed orders and at least 1 return have the highest refund ratios relative to their gross completed spend?
sql:
WITH customer_order_summary AS (
    SELECT 
        c.customer_id,
        c.first_name,
        c.last_name,
        c.email,
        c.loyalty_tier,
        r.name AS region_name,
        ca.city,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders,
        SUM(oi.line_total) AS total_gross_spend,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ret.return_id) AS total_returns,
        COALESCE(SUM(ret.refund_amount), 0.00) AS total_refunded
    FROM public.customers c
    JOIN public.regions r ON r.region_id = c.region_id
    JOIN public.customer_addresses ca ON ca.customer_id = c.customer_id AND ca.is_default = true
    JOIN public.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    LEFT JOIN public.returns ret ON ret.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'completed'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, c.email, c.loyalty_tier, r.name, ca.city
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) >= 3 AND COUNT(DISTINCT ret.return_id) >= 1
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    first_name || ' ' || last_name AS customer_name,
    email,
    loyalty_tier,
    region_name,
    city,
    total_orders,
    ROUND(total_gross_spend, 2) AS total_gross_spend,
    total_returns,
    ROUND(total_refunded, 2) AS total_refunded,
    ROUND((total_refunded / NULLIF(total_gross_spend, 0) * 100), 2) AS refund_ratio_pct
FROM customer_order_summary
ORDER BY refund_ratio_pct DESC, total_gross_spend DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests 6-table join across customer profile, primary shipping address, orders, items, and returns with HAVING aggregations.

question: What are the top 10 suppliers by net sales, showing their active inventory valuation, gross sales, and net revenue after refunds?
sql:
WITH supplier_inventory AS (
    SELECT 
        p.supplier_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS products_count,
        SUM(il.quantity_on_hand * p.unit_cost) AS total_inventory_valuation
    FROM public.products p
    JOIN public.product_variants pv ON pv.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN public.inventory_levels il ON il.variant_id = pv.variant_id
    WHERE p.status = 'active'
    GROUP BY p.supplier_id
),
supplier_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        p.supplier_id,
        SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold,
        SUM(oi.line_total) AS gross_sales,
        COALESCE(SUM(ret.refund_amount), 0.00) AS total_refunds
    FROM public.products p
    JOIN public.product_variants pv ON pv.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON oi.variant_id = pv.variant_id
    LEFT JOIN public.returns ret ON ret.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
    GROUP BY p.supplier_id
)
SELECT 
    s.supplier_id,
    s.company_name,
    s.country,
    s.rating AS supplier_rating,
    s.payment_terms,
    si.products_count,
    ROUND(si.total_inventory_valuation, 2) AS inventory_valuation_usd,
    ss.units_sold,
    ROUND(ss.gross_sales, 2) AS gross_sales_usd,
    ROUND(ss.gross_sales - ss.total_refunds, 2) AS net_sales_usd,
    ROUND((ss.total_refunds / NULLIF(ss.gross_sales, 0) * 100), 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM public.suppliers s
JOIN supplier_inventory si ON si.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
JOIN supplier_sales ss ON ss.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
ORDER BY net_sales_usd DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests 7-table graph resolving two independent aggregation branches (inventory valuation vs fulfilled order revenue with returns) combined via CTEs.

question: For the top 10 warehouses by total dispatched shipments, what are their active staffing levels, total payroll costs, facility capacity, delivered shipment count, avg delivery days, and on-time delivery rates?
sql:
WITH warehouse_labor AS (
    SELECT 
        w.warehouse_id,
        w.warehouse_code,
        w.name AS warehouse_name,
        r.name AS region_name,
        w.capacity_sqft,
        COUNT(e.employee_id) AS active_headcount,
        COALESCE(SUM(e.salary), 0.00) AS total_payroll
    FROM public.warehouses w
    JOIN public.regions r ON r.region_id = w.region_id
    LEFT JOIN public.employees e ON e.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id AND e.is_active = true
    GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.warehouse_code, w.name, r.name, w.capacity_sqft
),
warehouse_shipping AS (
    SELECT 
        s.warehouse_id,
        COUNT(s.shipment_id) AS total_dispatched,
        ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at)) / 86400), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
        ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN s.delivered_at::date <= s.estimated_delivery THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(s.shipment_id), 0) * 100, 2) AS on_time_rate_pct
    FROM public.shipments s
    WHERE s.shipment_status = 'delivered' AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY s.warehouse_id
)
SELECT 
    wl.warehouse_code,
    wl.warehouse_name,
    wl.region_name,
    wl.capacity_sqft,
    wl.active_headcount,
    ROUND(wl.total_payroll, 2) AS total_payroll_usd,
    COALESCE(ws.total_dispatched, 0) AS total_dispatched_shipments,
    ws.avg_delivery_days,
    ws.on_time_rate_pct
FROM warehouse_labor wl
LEFT JOIN warehouse_shipping ws ON ws.warehouse_id = wl.warehouse_id
ORDER BY total_dispatched_shipments DESC, on_time_rate_pct DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests operational cross-analysis joining warehouse physical assets, labor payrolls, and logistics delivery performance.

question: What is the settlement reconciliation across payment gateways and payment methods, including total transactions, captured volume, failed transactions, refund deductions, and failure percentage?
sql:
WITH order_refunds AS (
    SELECT 
        oi.order_id,
        COALESCE(SUM(ret.refund_amount), 0.00) AS total_refund_amount
    FROM public.order_items oi
    JOIN public.returns ret ON ret.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
    GROUP BY oi.order_id
)
SELECT 
    p.gateway_name,
    p.payment_method,
    COUNT(p.payment_id) AS total_transactions,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN p.payment_status = 'captured' THEN 1 END) AS successful_transactions,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN p.payment_status = 'failed' THEN 1 END) AS failed_transactions,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_status = 'captured' THEN p.amount ELSE 0.00 END), 2) AS gross_captured_usd,
    ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(orf.total_refund_amount), 0.00), 2) AS total_refunds_usd,
    ROUND(
        SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_status = 'captured' THEN p.amount ELSE 0.00 END) 
        - COALESCE(SUM(orf.total_refund_amount), 0.00), 
        2
    ) AS net_settled_usd,
    ROUND(
        COUNT(CASE WHEN p.payment_status = 'failed' THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(p.payment_id), 0) * 100, 
        2
    ) AS failure_rate_pct
FROM public.payments p
LEFT JOIN order_refunds orf ON orf.order_id = p.order_id
GROUP BY p.gateway_name, p.payment_method
ORDER BY gross_captured_usd DESC
notes: Tests payment transaction ledger reconciliation with item-level returns and conditional status aggregation.

question: Which top 10 high-value customers with over $1,500 in completed order spend and no orders in the last 60 days have paused or cancelled subscriptions and high or urgent support tickets?
sql:
SELECT 
    c.customer_id,
    c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name,
    c.email,
    c.loyalty_tier,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS completed_orders,
    ROUND(SUM(o.total_amount), 2) AS total_lifetime_spend,
    MAX(o.order_date) AS most_recent_order,
    COUNT(DISTINCT st.ticket_id) AS urgent_support_tickets,
    s.status AS subscription_status,
    s.billing_amount AS subscription_amount
FROM public.customers c
JOIN public.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_status = 'completed'
JOIN public.support_tickets st ON st.customer_id = c.customer_id AND st.priority IN ('high', 'urgent')
JOIN public.subscriptions s ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id AND s.status IN ('paused', 'cancelled')
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, c.email, c.loyalty_tier, s.status, s.billing_amount
HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) >= 1500
   AND MAX(o.order_date) <= NOW() - INTERVAL '60 days'
ORDER BY total_lifetime_spend DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests multi-domain join linking orders, subscriptions, and customer service tickets with recency and spend filters.

question: What are the top 10 promotions by net revenue on completed orders, showing their gross sales, total discount cost, net revenue, and average rating of products purchased?
sql:
WITH promo_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        pr.promotion_id,
        pr.promo_code,
        pr.discount_type,
        pr.discount_value,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders,
        SUM(o.subtotal_amount) AS gross_subtotal,
        SUM(o.discount_amount) AS total_discount_given,
        SUM(o.total_amount) AS net_revenue
    FROM public.promotions pr
    JOIN public.orders o ON o.promotion_id = pr.promotion_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'completed'
    GROUP BY pr.promotion_id, pr.promo_code, pr.discount_type, pr.discount_value
),
promo_reviews AS (
    SELECT 
        o.promotion_id,
        COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS items_purchased,
        ROUND(AVG(rev.rating), 2) AS avg_product_rating
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN public.product_variants pv ON pv.variant_id = oi.variant_id
    JOIN public.products p ON p.product_id = pv.product_id
    LEFT JOIN public.product_reviews rev ON rev.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'completed' AND o.promotion_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY o.promotion_id
)
SELECT 
    po.promo_code,
    po.discount_type,
    po.discount_value,
    po.total_orders,
    ROUND(po.gross_subtotal, 2) AS gross_subtotal_usd,
    ROUND(po.total_discount_given, 2) AS total_discount_given_usd,
    ROUND(po.net_revenue, 2) AS net_revenue_usd,
    prv.items_purchased,
    prv.avg_product_rating
FROM promo_orders po
JOIN promo_reviews prv ON prv.promotion_id = po.promotion_id
ORDER BY po.net_revenue DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests 6-table join graph evaluating marketing promotional efficacy against product quality reviews.

question: What is the carrier delivery SLA performance for the top 10 regional routes with at least 10 delivered shipments between origin warehouse regions and destination customer regions?
sql:
SELECT 
    s.carrier_name,
    orig_r.name AS origin_region,
    dest_r.name AS destination_region,
    COUNT(s.shipment_id) AS total_shipments,
    ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at)) / 86400), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN s.delivered_at::date > s.estimated_delivery THEN 1 END) AS delayed_shipments,
    ROUND(
        COUNT(CASE WHEN s.delivered_at::date <= s.estimated_delivery THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(s.shipment_id), 0) * 100, 
        2
    ) AS on_time_rate_pct
FROM public.shipments s
JOIN public.warehouses w ON w.warehouse_id = s.warehouse_id
JOIN public.regions orig_r ON orig_r.region_id = w.region_id
JOIN public.orders o ON o.order_id = s.order_id
JOIN public.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN public.regions dest_r ON dest_r.region_id = c.region_id
WHERE s.shipment_status = 'delivered' AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.carrier_name, orig_r.name, dest_r.name
HAVING COUNT(s.shipment_id) >= 10
ORDER BY total_shipments DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests dual join of the regions table (origin warehouse region vs destination customer region) requiring distinct table aliasing.

question: Which top 10 inventory positions in active warehouses have stock currently below safety stock, ordered by largest deficit units, along with their estimated replenishment cost per supplier?
sql:
SELECT 
    w.warehouse_code,
    w.name AS warehouse_name,
    r.name AS region_name,
    p.name AS product_name,
    pv.sku_variant,
    c.name AS category_name,
    s.company_name AS supplier_name,
    il.quantity_on_hand,
    il.safety_stock,
    (il.safety_stock - il.quantity_on_hand) AS deficit_units,
    ROUND((il.safety_stock - il.quantity_on_hand) * p.unit_cost, 2) AS replenishment_cost_usd
FROM public.inventory_levels il
JOIN public.warehouses w ON w.warehouse_id = il.warehouse_id
JOIN public.regions r ON r.region_id = w.region_id
JOIN public.product_variants pv ON pv.variant_id = il.variant_id
JOIN public.products p ON p.product_id = pv.product_id
JOIN public.categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
JOIN public.suppliers s ON s.supplier_id = p.supplier_id
WHERE il.quantity_on_hand < il.safety_stock AND w.status = 'active'
ORDER BY deficit_units DESC, replenishment_cost_usd DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests wide 7-table join through the supply chain graph from inventory positions to warehouses, regions, variants, products, categories, and suppliers.

question: What is the cohort breakdown of customer lifetime value, average review rating, and active subscription rate by loyalty tier and customer status?
sql:
WITH customer_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        c.customer_id,
        c.loyalty_tier,
        c.customer_status,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders_count,
        COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amount), 0.00) AS lifetime_spend,
        AVG(pr.rating) AS avg_rating_given,
        CASE WHEN EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM public.subscriptions s 
            WHERE s.customer_id = c.customer_id AND s.status = 'active'
        ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_active_subscription
    FROM public.customers c
    LEFT JOIN public.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_status = 'completed'
    LEFT JOIN public.product_reviews pr ON pr.customer_id = c.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.loyalty_tier, c.customer_status
)
SELECT 
    loyalty_tier,
    customer_status,
    COUNT(customer_id) AS total_customers,
    SUM(orders_count) AS total_completed_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(lifetime_spend), 2) AS avg_lifetime_value_usd,
    ROUND(SUM(lifetime_spend), 2) AS total_revenue_usd,
    ROUND(AVG(avg_rating_given), 2) AS avg_review_score,
    ROUND(SUM(has_active_subscription)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(customer_id), 0) * 100, 2) AS active_subscription_rate_pct
FROM customer_metrics
GROUP BY loyalty_tier, customer_status
ORDER BY total_revenue_usd DESC
notes: Tests customer cohort segmentation with correlated subquery EXISTS and multi-table metric rollups.

question: What is the support resolution performance by category and priority, including average resolution hours and linked customer refund amounts?
sql:
WITH ticket_order_refunds AS (
    SELECT 
        st.ticket_id,
        st.category,
        st.priority,
        st.status,
        st.created_at,
        st.resolved_at,
        COALESCE(SUM(ret.refund_amount), 0.00) AS linked_refund_amount
    FROM public.support_tickets st
    LEFT JOIN public.orders o ON o.order_id = st.order_id
    LEFT JOIN public.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    LEFT JOIN public.returns ret ON ret.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
    GROUP BY st.ticket_id, st.category, st.priority, st.status, st.created_at, st.resolved_at
)
SELECT 
    category,
    priority,
    COUNT(ticket_id) AS total_tickets,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN status IN ('resolved', 'closed') THEN 1 END) AS resolved_tickets_count,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN status IN ('open', 'in_progress') THEN 1 END) AS open_tickets_count,
    ROUND(
        AVG(CASE WHEN resolved_at IS NOT NULL 
            THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at)) / 3600 
            ELSE NULL END), 
        2
    ) AS avg_resolution_hours,
    ROUND(SUM(linked_refund_amount), 2) AS total_linked_refunds_usd
FROM ticket_order_refunds
GROUP BY category, priority
ORDER BY total_tickets DESC, open_tickets_count DESC
notes: Tests support escalation resolution times joined to downstream customer returns and order items.

question: What are the 10 most recent audit log entries for order status changes and price overrides on orders over $750, along with customer region and payment status?
sql:
SELECT 
    al.log_id,
    al.action,
    al.performed_by,
    al.created_at AS audit_timestamp,
    o.order_number,
    o.order_status,
    o.total_amount AS order_total,
    c.email AS customer_email,
    r.name AS customer_region,
    p.gateway_name,
    p.payment_status
FROM public.audit_logs al
JOIN public.orders o ON o.order_id = al.entity_id
JOIN public.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN public.regions r ON r.region_id = c.region_id
JOIN public.payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE al.entity_name = 'orders'
  AND al.action IN ('STATUS_CHANGE', 'PRICE_OVERRIDE')
  AND o.total_amount > 750
ORDER BY al.created_at DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests polymorphic audit log entity linkage joined across orders, customer profiles, regional geography, and payment settlement status.

question: Which top 10 customers with completed orders across at least 3 distinct top-level categories have the highest spend, and what is their top category by spend?
sql:
WITH customer_category_spend AS (
    SELECT 
        c.customer_id,
        c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name,
        c.email,
        COALESCE(pcat.name, cat.name) AS parent_category,
        SUM(oi.line_total) AS category_spend,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY c.customer_id 
            ORDER BY SUM(oi.line_total) DESC
        ) AS rank_in_customer
    FROM public.customers c
    JOIN public.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN public.product_variants pv ON pv.variant_id = oi.variant_id
    JOIN public.products p ON p.product_id = pv.product_id
    JOIN public.categories cat ON cat.category_id = p.category_id
    LEFT JOIN public.categories pcat ON pcat.category_id = cat.parent_category_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'completed'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, c.email, COALESCE(pcat.name, cat.name)
),
customer_summary AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        customer_name,
        email,
        COUNT(DISTINCT parent_category) AS distinct_parent_categories,
        SUM(category_spend) AS total_spend
    FROM customer_category_spend
    GROUP BY customer_id, customer_name, email
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT parent_category) >= 3
)
SELECT 
    cs.customer_id,
    cs.customer_name,
    cs.email,
    cs.distinct_parent_categories,
    ROUND(cs.total_spend, 2) AS total_spend_usd,
    ccs.parent_category AS top_category_by_spend,
    ROUND(ccs.category_spend, 2) AS top_category_spend_usd
FROM customer_summary cs
JOIN customer_category_spend ccs ON ccs.customer_id = cs.customer_id AND ccs.rank_in_customer = 1
ORDER BY cs.distinct_parent_categories DESC, cs.total_spend DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests 6-table join with ROW_NUMBER() window partitioning to identify customer primary preference categories amidst multi-category diversification.

question: For our top 10 products generating at least $10,000 in completed order revenue ordered by net revenue, what are their unit profit margins, total units sold, gross revenue, refund amounts, and average review ratings?
sql:
WITH product_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        p.product_id,
        p.name AS product_name,
        c.name AS category_name,
        s.company_name AS supplier_name,
        ROUND((p.unit_price - p.unit_cost), 2) AS unit_margin,
        SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold,
        SUM(oi.line_total) AS gross_revenue,
        COALESCE(SUM(ret.refund_amount), 0.00) AS total_refunds
    FROM public.products p
    JOIN public.categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
    JOIN public.suppliers s ON s.supplier_id = p.supplier_id
    JOIN public.product_variants pv ON pv.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON oi.variant_id = pv.variant_id
    JOIN public.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id AND o.order_status = 'completed'
    LEFT JOIN public.returns ret ON ret.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
    GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name, c.name, s.company_name, p.unit_price, p.unit_cost
    HAVING SUM(oi.line_total) >= 10000
),
product_ratings AS (
    SELECT 
        pr.product_id,
        COUNT(pr.review_id) AS review_count,
        ROUND(AVG(pr.rating), 2) AS avg_rating
    FROM public.product_reviews pr
    GROUP BY pr.product_id
)
SELECT 
    ps.product_name,
    ps.category_name,
    ps.supplier_name,
    ps.unit_margin AS unit_margin_usd,
    ps.total_units_sold,
    ROUND(ps.gross_revenue, 2) AS gross_revenue_usd,
    ROUND(ps.total_refunds, 2) AS total_refunds_usd,
    ROUND(ps.gross_revenue - ps.total_refunds, 2) AS net_revenue_usd,
    pr.avg_rating,
    COALESCE(pr.review_count, 0) AS total_reviews
FROM product_sales ps
LEFT JOIN product_ratings pr ON pr.product_id = ps.product_id
ORDER BY net_revenue_usd DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests comprehensive 8-table join analyzing net product profit margins against consumer satisfaction reviews.

question: For repeat customers, what is the average interval in days between consecutive completed orders by loyalty tier?
sql:
WITH order_gaps AS (
    SELECT 
        o.customer_id,
        c.loyalty_tier,
        o.order_date,
        LAG(o.order_date) OVER (
            PARTITION BY o.customer_id 
            ORDER BY o.order_date
        ) AS previous_order_date,
        o.total_amount
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'completed'
),
customer_intervals AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        loyalty_tier,
        AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (order_date - previous_order_date)) / 86400) AS avg_days_between_orders,
        SUM(total_amount) AS customer_spend
    FROM order_gaps
    WHERE previous_order_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY customer_id, loyalty_tier
)
SELECT 
    loyalty_tier,
    COUNT(customer_id) AS repeat_customer_count,
    ROUND(AVG(avg_days_between_orders), 1) AS avg_reorder_interval_days,
    ROUND(AVG(customer_spend), 2) AS avg_repeat_customer_spend_usd
FROM customer_intervals
GROUP BY loyalty_tier
ORDER BY avg_repeat_customer_spend_usd DESC
notes: Tests time-series inter-purchase cycle calculation using LAG() window function partitioned per customer.

question: Which top 10 suppliers with at least 50 total units sold have the highest defect return rates for items returned due to defective hardware or wrong sizing?
sql:
WITH supplier_units AS (
    SELECT 
        s.supplier_id,
        s.company_name,
        s.country,
        s.rating AS supplier_rating,
        SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold,
        SUM(oi.line_total) AS total_fulfilled_value
    FROM public.suppliers s
    JOIN public.products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
    JOIN public.product_variants pv ON pv.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON oi.variant_id = pv.variant_id
    GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.company_name, s.country, s.rating
),
supplier_defect_returns AS (
    SELECT 
        p.supplier_id,
        COUNT(r.return_id) AS defect_returns_count,
        COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_amount), 0.00) AS defect_refunds_usd
    FROM public.products p
    JOIN public.product_variants pv ON pv.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON oi.variant_id = pv.variant_id
    JOIN public.returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
    WHERE r.return_reason IN ('defective_hardware', 'wrong_size_color')
    GROUP BY p.supplier_id
)
SELECT 
    su.supplier_id,
    su.company_name,
    su.country,
    su.supplier_rating,
    su.total_units_sold,
    ROUND(su.total_fulfilled_value, 2) AS fulfilled_value_usd,
    COALESCE(sdr.defect_returns_count, 0) AS defect_returns_count,
    ROUND(COALESCE(sdr.defect_refunds_usd, 0.00), 2) AS defect_refunds_usd,
    ROUND(
        COALESCE(sdr.defect_returns_count, 0)::numeric / NULLIF(su.total_units_sold, 0) * 100, 
        2
    ) AS defect_return_rate_pct
FROM supplier_units su
LEFT JOIN supplier_defect_returns sdr ON sdr.supplier_id = su.supplier_id
WHERE su.total_units_sold >= 50
ORDER BY defect_return_rate_pct DESC, defect_refunds_usd DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests 5-table supply chain traversal isolating defective hardware return rates across upstream manufacturers.

question: For each shipping carrier, what is the rate of support tickets filed for delivery delays and the volume of logistics-related returns?
sql:
WITH carrier_tickets AS (
    SELECT 
        s.carrier_name,
        COUNT(DISTINCT s.shipment_id) AS delivered_shipments,
        COUNT(DISTINCT st.ticket_id) AS delivery_support_tickets
    FROM public.shipments s
    LEFT JOIN public.support_tickets st ON st.order_id = s.order_id 
        AND st.category IN ('order_tracking', 'delivery_delay')
    WHERE s.shipment_status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY s.carrier_name
),
carrier_returns AS (
    SELECT 
        s.carrier_name,
        COUNT(DISTINCT r.return_id) AS logistics_returns_count,
        COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_amount), 0.00) AS logistics_refunds_usd
    FROM public.shipments s
    JOIN public.orders o ON o.order_id = s.order_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN public.returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id 
        AND r.return_reason IN ('arrived_late', 'defective_hardware')
    WHERE s.shipment_status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY s.carrier_name
)
SELECT 
    ct.carrier_name,
    ct.delivered_shipments,
    ct.delivery_support_tickets,
    ROUND(ct.delivery_support_tickets::numeric / NULLIF(ct.delivered_shipments, 0) * 100, 2) AS ticket_rate_pct,
    COALESCE(cr.logistics_returns_count, 0) AS logistics_returns_count,
    ROUND(COALESCE(cr.logistics_refunds_usd, 0.00), 2) AS logistics_refunds_usd
FROM carrier_tickets ct
LEFT JOIN carrier_returns cr ON cr.carrier_name = ct.carrier_name
ORDER BY ct.delivered_shipments DESC
notes: Tests multi-branch join combining shipping records with support ticket complaints and return refunds.

question: Segment our customers into monetary quartiles based on their lifetime spending, showing average spend, order count, and recency in days for each quartile.
sql:
WITH customer_rfm AS (
    SELECT 
        c.customer_id,
        c.loyalty_tier,
        r.name AS region_name,
        COUNT(o.order_id) AS frequency,
        ROUND(SUM(o.total_amount), 2) AS monetary_value,
        ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - MAX(o.order_date))) / 86400, 1) AS recency_days,
        NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY SUM(o.total_amount) DESC) AS monetary_quartile,
        NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(o.order_id) DESC) AS frequency_quartile,
        NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY MAX(o.order_date) DESC) AS recency_quartile
    FROM public.customers c
    JOIN public.regions r ON r.region_id = c.region_id
    JOIN public.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'completed'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.loyalty_tier, r.name
)
SELECT 
    monetary_quartile,
    COUNT(customer_id) AS customer_count,
    ROUND(AVG(monetary_value), 2) AS avg_monetary_usd,
    ROUND(AVG(frequency), 2) AS avg_order_frequency,
    ROUND(AVG(recency_days), 1) AS avg_recency_days
FROM customer_rfm
GROUP BY monetary_quartile
ORDER BY monetary_quartile ASC
notes: Tests advanced statistical NTILE(4) quartile distribution across customer lifetime spending and order recency.

question: What is the subscription churn rate and active monthly recurring revenue across top-level product categories, along with average customer support tickets?
sql:
WITH sub_tickets AS (
    SELECT 
        s.subscription_id,
        s.customer_id,
        s.product_id,
        s.status,
        s.billing_amount,
        COUNT(st.ticket_id) AS ticket_count
    FROM public.subscriptions s
    LEFT JOIN public.support_tickets st ON st.customer_id = s.customer_id
    GROUP BY s.subscription_id, s.customer_id, s.product_id, s.status, s.billing_amount
)
SELECT 
    COALESCE(pcat.name, cat.name) AS parent_category,
    COUNT(st.subscription_id) AS total_subscriptions,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN st.status = 'active' THEN 1 END) AS active_subscriptions,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN st.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled_subscriptions,
    ROUND(
        COUNT(CASE WHEN st.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(st.subscription_id), 0) * 100, 
        2
    ) AS churn_rate_pct,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN st.status = 'active' THEN st.billing_amount ELSE 0.00 END), 2) AS active_mrr_usd,
    ROUND(AVG(st.ticket_count), 2) AS avg_support_tickets_per_subscriber
FROM sub_tickets st
JOIN public.products p ON p.product_id = st.product_id
JOIN public.categories cat ON cat.category_id = p.category_id
LEFT JOIN public.categories pcat ON pcat.category_id = cat.parent_category_id
GROUP BY COALESCE(pcat.name, cat.name)
ORDER BY active_mrr_usd DESC
notes: Tests SaaS recurring revenue and churn metrics mapped to parent categories and support ticket correlation.

question: Which top 10 suppliers by total units on hand have products distributed across at least 5 active warehouses with an average safety stock over 20 units, and what is their total inventory volume?
sql:
SELECT 
    s.supplier_id,
    s.company_name,
    s.country,
    s.rating AS supplier_rating,
    s.payment_terms,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS distinct_products_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT pv.variant_id) AS distinct_variants_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT il.warehouse_id) AS warehouse_coverage_count,
    SUM(il.quantity_on_hand) AS total_units_on_hand,
    ROUND(AVG(p.unit_cost), 2) AS avg_product_cost_usd,
    ROUND(AVG(il.safety_stock), 1) AS avg_safety_stock
FROM public.suppliers s
JOIN public.products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
JOIN public.product_variants pv ON pv.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN public.inventory_levels il ON il.variant_id = pv.variant_id
JOIN public.warehouses w ON w.warehouse_id = il.warehouse_id AND w.status = 'active'
GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.company_name, s.country, s.rating, s.payment_terms
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT il.warehouse_id) >= 5
   AND AVG(il.safety_stock) > 20
ORDER BY total_units_on_hand DESC, supplier_rating DESC
LIMIT 10
notes: Tests supply chain distribution coverage requiring multiple distinct counts and aggregate threshold conditions in HAVING clause.
